title: Wilma Rudolph's birth chart
metaDescription: Wilma Rudolph's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 2.0° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Cancer — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Mars. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 2.0° Cancer — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Moon. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Cancer and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 27.3° Cancer, Venus was at 7.0° Cancer, Mars was at 23.8° Cancer. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mars to Uranus, a sextile with 0.5° of slack. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Mars sextile Neptune at 1.0°, and Venus sextile Jupiter at 1.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: One planet here sits in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mars in Cancer at 23.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 water, 4 earth, 1 air, 1 fire; by modality, 5 fixed, 4 cardinal, 1 mutable. Venus was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.4° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 17.2°.
